source.title: High-dimensional ridgeless least squares interpolation under spiked covariance structures

record.tranche_reason: It analyzes double-descent-related prediction-risk curves using asymptotic theory for ridgeless linear regression, rather than the original deep-network setting.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own risk-curve results for aspect ratio and spiked-covariance conditions. Cited results from other work are not recorded. Simulation parameter choices and figure captions without an explicitly described outcome are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: It derives and plots the asymptotic risk of the min-norm interpolator against aspect ratio γ=p/n under spiked covariance. This is a new setting (non-isotropic linear regression) with its own results on whether risk improves past the interpolation threshold (V4). Not T1/T2: no deep networks, and not a replication of the originals' method.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the number, strength and alignment of spikes jointly govern the min-norm interpolator's risk and the double-descent curve. Specifically: alignment between β and spike directions is detrimental and can destroy benign overparameterization, yielding tempered or catastrophic overfitting. Orthogonal targets recover isotropic or benign behaviour.
record.recipe_differences: Asymptotic analysis and simulations of ridgeless least-squares regression under spiked covariance; it does not use the original deep-network setting.
record.method_sensitivity: Risk-curve behavior varies with spike strength and target-spike alignment; the authors also report dependence on SNR.

fits_no_version.finding: The overfitting regime as γ→∞ is benign, tempered or catastrophic depending on target-spike alignment and on the growth rate of Σαj/p relative to γ (Theorem 4.1, Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether overparameterized interpolation generalizes depends on alignment between the target and the high-variance covariance directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Risk rises linearly with the squared alignment ⟨u1,β⟩² (Fig 4, M=1, α1=20, SNR=2.33).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Signal alignment with spiked directions harms min-norm interpolation risk.

record.problems: The reported curve descriptions are qualitative rather than tabulated exact risk values. Figure 5(b) has an inconsistency: the prose gives a spike sum of 500, while its caption gives 200.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows left out.

untested.parts: No deep networks or model-size sweeps.
γ is varied by changing n at fixed p, but the paper never frames or reports any result as more samples raising risk near interpolation.

Only ridgeless linear regression is studied, not multiple model classes. The classical U-shape in the underparameterized regime is not examined, since the risk there is σ²γ/(1−γ), monotone increasing.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
SNR effects on the curve are described, but noise is not tested as the driver of the peak. No multiple peaks. No regularization, since the estimator is ridgeless only.

missing.what: Theoretical limits showing the interpolation peak. For γ<1 the risk σ²γ/(1−γ) grows toward γ=1. For γ>1 the variance term σ²/(γ−1) diverges as γ→1⁺. Together these give the double-descent peak at the threshold.
Statement that for γ>1 the null-estimator risk beats the spiked interpolator's risk curves for SNR 1–5.
Asymptotic regime results (benign/tempered/catastrophic) as γ→∞ by alignment and spike growth rate. These bear on whether risk keeps improving with overparameterization.
Risk grows linearly with spike sum at fixed γ>1, and the bias term dominates (Figs 2–3).

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: this is a new setting (spiked-covariance linear regression), not a different method aimed at the deep-network question. γ is varied with p fixed at 300 and n=p/γ, so the 'capacity' axis is really the ratio p/n. All results are asymptotic formulas and noiseless deterministic curves, with no uncertainty reported. There is a Fig 5(b) spike-sum inconsistency (500 in the prose vs 200 in the caption). The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Changing the number of training samples near interpolation.
The study considers ridgeless linear regression, not multiple model classes; its results concern the aspect ratio and specified covariance and signal-alignment settings.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and sample size.
Whether noise drives the peak, whether peaks split, and whether optimally tuned regularization removes them.
Whether an effective-parameter count turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: min-norm least squares estimator under the generalized spiked covariance model
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed asymptotic prediction risk as the aspect ratio γ and the sum of spiked eigenvalues varied.

conditions.value: Σ from M=1 to M αi varied

rows.value: For γ>1, risk has a U-shaped trend, first decreasing and then increasing. As the spike sum grows, the minimum occurs earlier and is higher.
rows.note: The text describes the risk surface and its cross-sections qualitatively; it gives no exact risk values.
rows.check: For γ>1 the risk falls after the interpolation point, then rises again, with a minimum that grows with spike sum. The improvement past interpolation is real but short-lived, so 'observed' overstates it. Conditions: SNR=2.33, σ²=1, ⟨ui,β⟩=1 (Fig 2 caption), not ⟨ui,β⟩²=1 as a separate key.

rows.subject: min-norm least squares estimator under the spiked covariance model
rows.operation_detail: Compared risk curves over aspect ratio γ for a spiked covariance setting.
rows.measure: Prediction risk as a function of γ
rows.value: The spiked risk curve reaches its minimum earlier than in the isotropic case and then rebounds rapidly; its minimum is higher than the isotropic minimum.
rows.note: Qualitative curve comparison stated in the text; exact plotted values are not given.
rows.check: Second descent is present but the curve reaches its minimum earlier and rebounds rapidly, at a higher minimum than isotropic. Text also says the null risk beats the risk curves for γ>1; the record omits this. Downgrade from observed.

rows.subject: min-norm least squares estimator under the spiked covariance model
rows.operation_detail: Compared risk curves over aspect ratio γ for a stronger-spike setting.
rows.measure: Prediction risk as a function of γ
rows.baseline: Spiked setting with Σ αi=50, Figure 1(b)
rows.value: Larger spiked eigenvalues yield a higher minimum risk.
rows.note: The text reports the minimum-risk comparison but does not separately describe the full curve shape for this condition.
rows.check: Only the higher-minimum comparison versus Σαi=50 is stated. Consistent with a further weakened second descent; state acceptable.

rows.subject: min-norm least squares estimator under the spiked covariance model
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed asymptotic risk curves over aspect ratio γ with the target orthogonal to the spike directions.
rows.measure: Asymptotic prediction risk as a function of γ
rows.value: The risk is the same as in the isotropic case when the spike sum is treated as o(p).
rows.note: The prose identifies the spike sum as 50; the figure caption also gives 50.
rows.check: Risk equals the isotropic case (Hastie et al. 2022), which has the usual peak at γ=1 and descent beyond it. Baseline correct.

rows.subject: min-norm least squares estimator under the spiked covariance model
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed asymptotic risk curves over aspect ratio γ with the target orthogonal to the spike directions.
rows.measure: Asymptotic prediction risk as a function of γ
rows.baseline: Spiked setting with spike sum 50, Figure 5(a)
rows.value: The overall risk trends downward as γ increases.
rows.note: The prose says the spike sum is 500, but the Figure 5(b) caption says 200.
rows.check: Risk trends downward as γ grows: a sustained second descent. Spike sum is inconsistent: 500 in the prose, 200 in the Fig 5 caption. Treat the condition as uncertain.

relationships.condition: Target orthogonal to spike directions (⟨β,ui⟩=0), p=300, M=5
relationships.reason: Risk past γ=1 matches the isotropic double-descent curve at small spike sum (r4). With a large spike sum it decreases steadily as γ grows (r5).
relationships.display_finding: Beyond γ = 1, risk matched the isotropic double-descent curve for a small spike sum and decreased steadily with γ for a large spike sum.

relationships.condition: Target aligned with spike directions (⟨β,ui⟩≠0), spike sums 30–200, SNR 1–5
relationships.reason: A second descent appears after γ=1 but bottoms out early, at a higher minimum that grows with spike strength, then rebounds (r1, r2, r3). Authors say spikes can destroy benign overparameterization.
relationships.display_finding: Error declined after γ = 1 but reached an early minimum that increased with spike strength, then rebounded.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Spiked covariance settings with nonzero target-spike alignment; aspect ratio and spike strength varied
reader_labels.reason: The reported risk curve has a decreasing-then-increasing segment for γ>1, with its minimum shifting with spike strength (r1, r2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Target orthogonal to spike directions, especially the large-spike setting
reader_labels.reason: The curve behavior depends on alignment and spike strength: the low-spike case matches the isotropic risk, while the reported high-spike case trends downward as γ grows (r4, r5).
